title: Daily Temperatures
statement: You get a list of daily temperatures. For each day, report how many days you must wait until a strictly warmer day. If no warmer day ever comes, report 0 for that day.

example.caption: Day 0 is 73. The next day is 74, so it waits 1. Day 2 is 75 and waits 4 days for 76.

idea.sentence: Keep a stack of days that are still waiting. When a warmer day arrives, it ends the wait of every colder day on top of the stack.

jargon.plain: A stack whose items stay in one order, here falling temperature from bottom to top. Items that break the order are popped first.
A day's position in the list. The stack stores positions, so the wait is a simple subtraction.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a list of temperatures, e.g. [73,74,75,71,69,72,76,73]

compare.bruteLabel: For each day scan ahead for a warmer one

rows.name: Scan ahead
rows.note: A falling list makes every day scan to the end and find nothing.

rows.name: Monotonic stack
rows.note: Each day is pushed once and popped at most once, so the while loop costs n in total.

fast.takeaway: Do not search ahead. Let each day wait on the stack, and let the warmer day that arrives settle all of them at once.

stages.title: Setup
stages.note: answer is all zeros. The stack holds the days that have not found a warmer day yet.

stages.title: Warmer day pops
stages.note: While today is warmer than the day on top, pop that day. Its wait is today minus its index.

stages.title: Push today
stages.note: Today is not settled yet. It joins the stack and waits for something warmer.

stages.title: Leftovers
stages.note: Days still on the stack never found a warmer day. They keep 0.

edges.title: One day
edges.why: Nothing comes after it. It is pushed and never popped.

edges.title: Always falling
edges.why: No day is warmer than the top, so nothing ever pops. The stack grows to n.

edges.title: Equal temperatures
edges.why: Equal is not warmer. The first 70 keeps waiting until 71 shows up.

edges.title: Many settled at once
edges.why: The 80 pops three days in one go. That is why the loop inside is a while, not an if.

gotchas.text: Use > not >=. Equal days must stay on the stack.
Push the index, not the temperature. The answer needs the distance in days, and the temperature is one lookup away.
The inner loop must be a while. An if settles only one day and leaves colder ones stuck under today.
new Array(n).fill(0) gives numbers. new Array(n) alone is sparse and holds empty slots, not zeros.
make([]int, n) is already zero filled, which is exactly the default answer. Do not loop to fill it.
stack.pop() returns number | undefined. Inside the while the stack is not empty, so a ! assertion is safe there.

recap.key: Days wait on a stack. A warmer day pops every colder day it beats and answers them with its index distance.
moves: Answer starts as zeros, stack is empty
While today beats the top day, pop it and set its answer
Days left on the stack keep 0
